newsitem.title: UK: UK grains slide under currency, harvest pressure.
newsitem.headline: UK grains slide under currency, harvest pressure.

text.p: A strong pound sterling and bumper harvest put new pressure on LIFFE grain futures on Tuesday with wheat as much as 1.40 stg a tonne down at one point and a new contract low of 97.40 stg paid for November.
A new estimate by French cereals analyst Strategie Grains raised this year's European Union cereals harvest forecast by 2.5 million tonnes to a record 201.4 million tonnes.
The increase brings the private forecaster's estimate close to recently-published trade data and follow's upbeat crop reports from northern European and Scandinavian producers.
UK traders also could see no let up in the pressure on the London futures market which turned sharply down last week while sterling remains strong.
Traders said the market tried to bounce during Tuesday afternoon but soon ran out of steam.
"I think it was a short lead rally, but sterling soon put a stop to it," said a trader.
At the close wheat futures were 0.70 to 1.30 stg down on a turonver of 827 lots.
Barley finished one stg down after trading 21 lots.
In Amsterdam milling wheat futures closed unchanged and tradeless.
On the UK fob market Nov feed wheat fetched 102 stg, Jan/Mar 103.50 stg and Apr/Jun 105.25 stg a tonne all for 2,400 tonnes loads ex-east coast ports in coasters.
Delivered market traders reported mainly short covering with milling wheat 11 percent protein fetching 126 stg for Jan/Mar in Liverpool and 124 stg in Yorkshire.
Feed wheat in the Avon range traded at 101.50 and 100 stg for Oct while 101 stg was paid in East Anglia.
Nearby feed barley was fetching around 102.50 stg in the east and 102 and 102.50 stg in the middle of the country.
